correctness.rationale: Under irreducible B≥0, D positive, C² nonnegative responses φ_ij(0)=0 and ψ_ij(0)>0, link recovery ξ_ij>0, and R0=1, the compact feasible cube is forward invariant. The normalized left Perron mass W=lᵀy has the exact nonpositive derivative −∑l_i y_i(By)_i−∑l_i(1−y_i)β_ij y_j(1−z_ij). If a nonzero support were trapped in zero derivative, irreducibility supplies an outgoing infected-to-susceptible edge whose contact is open; that coordinate then becomes positive, contradicting maximal invariance. LaSalle therefore gives y→0, and strict zero-prevalence link restoration gives z→1. Because W>0 and W’/W=O(W+||1−z||)→0, W is slowly varying relative to every exponential kernel. Spectral projection for A=B−D, lᵀr=1 and ∑r=1 yields y/W→r. Link-deficit variation of constants gives (1−z_ij)/W→γ_ij=ζ_ij Dφ_ij(0)[r]/(ξ_ij ψ_ij(0)); substituting in W’ gives W’/W²→−κ, κ=∑l_i(δ_i r_i²+∑β_ij r_jγ_ij)>0. Hence tW→1/κ and the two claimed vector limits for all initial y(0)≠0. When all φ directional slopes vanish, the leading coefficient reduces exactly to static SIS. Boundary y(0)=0 is correctly excluded. Independently checked two-group rational coefficients c=0,1,2,5; finite trajectories are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The initiating 2024/2025 multigroup adaptive SIS paper proves strict R0<1 global stability, not equality, and its strong linear spectral-gap proof cannot establish the critical 1/t rate. A published one-community scalar theorem (same date) supplies a critical feedback-slope coefficient but requires one prevalence coordinate and monotone responses, and does not imply the stated n-group Perron-coupled all-initial-state theorem without additional analysis. Static critical SIS can give Perron decay but lacks evolving links and γ_ij. The precise κ and each link-deficit limit are the original mathematical object under assessed evidence; historical priority is best knowledge.
residual_risks: An unindexed multigroup critical center-manifold expansion may imply the coefficient κ under more general assumptions.

value.rationale: The sharp reproduction-number equality separates exponential extinction from nonlinear critical slowing and is a natural missing case of multigroup adaptive epidemic models. The explicit network-weighted 1/t amplitude measures how first-order contact avoidance changes late prevalence, whereas quadratic response does not. It resolves a full network-irreducible class (no monotonicity), rather than a tuned example or merely the already-known threshold.

limitations: Finite-dimensional deterministic system with irreducible B and positive zero-prevalence contact creation; no stochastic, reducible, infinite-network or supercritical result; first-order asymptotic only.
